definition: A situation test is a behavioural assessment used to examine attachment by observing how an individual responds to a caregiver and a stranger across separations and reunions in an unfamiliar or mildly stressful setting. In this context, it is used to judge whether the caregiver serves as a source of safety and security.

reasons: The definition adds unsupported procedural detail: the packet does not establish a standard sequence of separations and reunions in an unfamiliar or mildly stressful setting, nor does it clearly define the test in those terms.

The packet supports the idea of assessing whether a carer is perceived as a source of safety and security, but it does not support the broader generic framing of a ‘situation test’ as a general behavioural assessment beyond the specific Strange Situation Test context.

The packet supports that the Strange Situation Test is used to assess whether a primary carer is perceived as a focus of safety and security in otherwise threatening environments, but it does not explicitly state the procedure elements “across separations and reunions.”
The packet does not explicitly describe the setting as “unfamiliar or mildly stressful”; it only refers to “otherwise threatening environments.”

The packet contrasts “owner” and “stranger” (e.g., comparing effects when owner vs stranger leaves the cat), but it does not explicitly describe the full caregiver–stranger separation/reunion sequence implied by the definition.
